articles.headline: Gondán bota el Edda Fjord, el mayor buque de sus 101 años de historia
articles.subtitle: El astillero de Figueras, en Castropol, puso en el agua un barco de 125 metros de eslora, 23 de manga y unos 40 de altura, contratado por el armador noruego Østensjø Rederi y que se entregará a finales de 2027.
articles.body:
Los astilleros Gondán botaron este jueves en Figueras (Castropol) el Edda Fjord, el buque de mayores dimensiones construido en los 101 años de historia de la compañía. La maniobra se ejecutó a las cuatro de la tarde, aprovechando la pleamar y una ría del Eo en calma, y reunió a numeroso público en ambas orillas, desde la propia Figueras hasta varios puntos de Ribadeo.

El barco, al que en el astillero llaman Gondán Max, mide 125 metros de eslora, 23 de manga y más de 40 de altura. Está contratado por el armador noruego Østensjø Rederi, cliente histórico de la casa, que ya le ha encargado 23 embarcaciones. Otras informaciones, como las de La Voz de Asturias, rebajan la eslora a 120 metros y cifran en 173 las plazas.

## Apoyo a la eólica marina

Diseñado por la firma noruega Salt Ship Design, es un buque multiservicio para energías marinas: transporte seguro de personal, apoyo a parques eólicos, construcción offshore, inspección con vehículos operados remotamente y tendido y reparación de cables submarinos. Tendrá propulsión híbrida y acomodación para 180 personas.

La construcción, respaldada por una línea de avales de CaixaBank de más de 125 millones de euros, ha implicado a unos 400 trabajadores en distintas fases. Tras la botadura afronta el armamento a flote y las pruebas de mar, con entrega prevista para finales de 2027.

articles.headline: Institutos de Lugo arrancan el curso sin cafetería tras renunciar los concesionarios
articles.subtitle: Centros como el Muralla Romana, Ollos Grandes, Leiras Pulpeiro o el María Sarmiento de Viveiro abren sin este servicio. Los adjudicatarios citan la normativa estatal de alimentación saludable y el encarecimiento de las materias primas.
articles.body:
Varios institutos de la provincia de Lugo han empezado el curso sin servicio de cafetería después de que los adjudicatarios renunciasen a la concesión. Es el caso de los IES Muralla Romana, Ollos Grandes y Leiras Pulpeiro, en la capital, y del María Sarmiento de Viveiro, cuya cantina espera una nueva licitación. La situación se repite en Sarria, Guitiriz o Monterroso.

Los responsables de estos establecimientos apuntan a dos causas. La primera, la entrada en vigor el pasado abril de la normativa estatal de comedores saludables, que limita la venta de bollería industrial y bebidas azucaradas. La segunda, el encarecimiento de materias primas como huevos, patatas o aceite, con el bocadillo congelado en un máximo de 1,50 euros.

Víctor Rolle, que dejó la cafetería del María Sarmiento tras más de dos décadas, describe la nueva regulación como "a gota que colmou o vaso" y sostiene que la rentabilidad es "nula". Eva Carracedo, del IES Sanxillao, subraya además la función social del servicio: hay alumnos que llegan sin desayunar o sin dinero para hacerlo en el centro.

Desde la Consellería de Educación, la Xunta cifra en 47 las renuncias en Galicia, casi una de cada cuatro de las 200 cantinas escolares, y atribuye el problema a una norma estatal impuesta "sin ningún tipo de diálogo ni de financiación".

articles.headline: La búsqueda de la mujer desaparecida en Ponferrada se extiende por el Camino Francés
articles.subtitle: Sarria, Samos y Triacastela reparten carteles de María González Camuñas, de 82 años y vista por última vez en O Cebreiro, mientras la Guardia Civil mantiene el operativo con drones y batidas.
articles.body:
La búsqueda de María González Camuñas, la vecina de Ponferrada de 82 años desaparecida el pasado 2 de septiembre, se ha extendido a los concellos lucenses del Camino Francés. Sarria, Samos y Triacastela repartieron este jueves carteles con su fotografía y su descripción física, con la colaboración de los tres ayuntamientos.

La mujer fue vista por última vez en O Cebreiro, en el concello de Pedrafita do Cebreiro, en el límite con la comarca leonesa de El Bierzo, adonde se había desplazado en taxi. Ese detalle llevó a la Policía Nacional a trasladar las diligencias a la Comandancia de la Guardia Civil de Lugo.

En Sarria los carteles se colocaron en distintos puntos de la Rúa Maior, por donde pasan a diario cientos de peregrinos, y el Concello difundió la imagen en sus redes sociales. La Asociación de Amigos do Camiño de Santiago na Comarca de Sarria la distribuyó también entre sus contactos.

El operativo incluye batidas y drones en el entorno de O Cebreiro, un terreno de alta montaña de orografía complicada. La mujer mide 1,60 metros, tiene ojos verdes y pelo castaño, precisa medicación y vestía camisa blanca y pantalón vaquero azul cuando se le perdió la pista.

articles.headline: Marruecos exige a España que devuelva a los menores de Ceuta y niega ser "chivo expiatorio"
articles.subtitle: El Ministerio de Exteriores marroquí cuestiona en un duro comunicado por qué no se ha expulsado a los migrantes irregulares ni devuelto a los no acompañados, y lamenta que se le señale "sin pruebas".
articles.body:
El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Marruecos publicó este jueves un comunicado inusualmente duro en el que cuestiona que España no haya devuelto a los migrantes que entraron de forma irregular en Ceuta a finales de julio ni a los menores no acompañados que siguen en la ciudad autónoma.

"¿Por qué se mantiene la crítica contra Marruecos cuando ningún dato, ningún hecho ni ningún informe establece alguna implicación de las autoridades marroquíes?", se pregunta Rabat. El texto sostiene que se señala al reino alauí "sin pruebas" y advierte de que no acepta ser "chivo expiatorio" en ajustes de cuentas políticos en España ni "activo comercial en vísperas electorales".

## Ochenta mil entradas

Marruecos cifra en más de 80.000 las personas que cruzaron la frontera y reclama un "estudio profundo" de lo ocurrido para determinar sus causas, identificar a los actores implicados y evitar que se repita. La ministra de Defensa, Margarita Robles, defendió el jueves que la entrada fue "imprevisible", aunque admitió que "todo se puede hacer mejor".

Pese al tono, Rabat subraya que mantiene su relación de "buena vecindad" con España y cita la declaración conjunta de 2022 entre Mohamed VI y Pedro Sánchez como base de la "nueva etapa" bilateral. El Gobierno no ha respondido por ahora al comunicado.

articles.headline: El BCE sube los tipos al 2,5% y encarece otra vez las hipotecas variables
articles.subtitle: El Consejo de Gobierno eleva el precio del dinero 25 puntos básicos, su segundo incremento del año, por una inflación del 3,3% en la eurozona y un Brent por encima de los 100 dólares.
articles.body:
El Banco Central Europeo subió este jueves los tipos de interés 25 puntos básicos. La tasa de depósito queda en el 2,5%, la de las operaciones de refinanciación en el 2,65% y la facilidad marginal de préstamo en el 2,90%. Es el segundo incremento del año tras el de junio, el primero desde 2023, y estaba descontado por los mercados.

El motivo es la inflación: la eurozona cerró agosto en el 3,3%, frente al 2,9% de julio, con la energía disparada un 14,3% por las tensiones en el estrecho de Ormuz y la guerra entre Irán y Estados Unidos. Christine Lagarde calificó la decisión de "una obviedad", respaldada por unanimidad, y evitó orientar sobre los próximos pasos.

## Reacción inmediata en la deuda

El mercado reaccionó el mismo día. El bono español a diez años escaló al 3,963%, máximos desde 2023, y el alemán se situó en el 3,5%, niveles de 2011, según El Mundo. El think tank Funcas advierte de que unos tipos más altos estrechan el margen fiscal de los Estados y elevan la factura de intereses hasta unos 60.000 millones en 2030.

Para las familias españolas el efecto llega vía euríbor, al que están referenciadas la mayoría de las hipotecas variables. Los analistas no descartan una tercera subida en diciembre, hasta el 2,75%, si el shock energético se mantiene.

articles.headline: El Congreso aprueba la nacionalidad para los saharauis con el PP abstenido y Vox en contra
articles.subtitle: La proposición de ley de Sumar, pactada con el PSOE, concede la nacionalidad por carta de naturaleza a los nacidos antes del 29 de septiembre de 1977 y a sus descendientes; pasa ahora al Senado.
articles.body:
El Congreso aprobó este jueves la proposición de ley que concede la nacionalidad española a los saharauis nacidos cuando el Sáhara Occidental estaba bajo administración española y a sus descendientes directos. El texto salió adelante con los votos del PSOE, Sumar y sus socios, la abstención del PP, Junts y UPN y el rechazo de Vox, y continúa su tramitación en el Senado.

La norma, impulsada por Sumar y pactada después con el PSOE —que votó en contra en la toma en consideración—, invoca "circunstancias excepcionales" para conceder la nacionalidad por carta de naturaleza a los nacidos antes del 29 de septiembre de 1977, aunque no residan legalmente en España. Las solicitudes serán gratuitas y podrán presentarse durante tres años, ampliables uno más.

El PP defendió la vía de la residencia en lugar de la carta de naturaleza y sostuvo que la ley no ofrece garantías suficientes de aplicación. Vox fue el único grupo que votó en contra: argumenta que la nacionalidad "no puede ser una indemnización de hoy por la historia de ayer".

La votación llegó en plena tensión con Marruecos por la crisis de Ceuta y una semana después de que el Supremo suspendiera cautelarmente el voto de parte de los nacionalizados por la ley de nietos. Varios socios del Gobierno reprocharon al Ejecutivo su giro sobre el Sáhara de 2022.

articles.headline: La Diada llega con el independentismo fracturado y Aliança disparada en los sondeos
articles.subtitle: Los Mossos cargaron en la víspera contra grupos antifascistas que querían boicotear el acto de Aliança Catalana en el Fossar de les Moreres, mientras Sigma Dos sitúa a Orriols como segunda fuerza del Parlament.
articles.body:
La Diada de este viernes llega a Cataluña con el independentismo más dividido que en años. En la víspera, los Mossos d'Esquadra cargaron en el Fossar de les Moreres contra grupos antifascistas que pretendían impedir el acto de Aliança Catalana en ese espacio, escenario tradicional de la izquierda secesionista.

Arran, las juventudes de la CUP, había convocado a sus simpatizantes a ocupar el Fossar media hora antes del acto de la formación de Sílvia Orriols, con el argumento de no "regalar" el independentismo a un partido de discurso antiinmigración. Hubo cargas y momentos de tensión, sin incidentes graves.

Los datos demoscópicos explican el choque. Un sondeo de Sigma Dos para El Mundo otorga a Aliança entre 25 y 28 escaños, cuando en 2024 obtuvo dos, y la sitúa como segunda fuerza del Parlament y primera entre los independentistas, por delante de Junts, que perdería hasta 13 diputados, y de ERC. El PSC seguiría ganando, pero Illa caería de 42 a 31-33 escaños.

El president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa, apeló en su mensaje institucional a la "unidad de país" y a preservar la convivencia: "El odio no tiene cabida". La marcha independentista de este viernes aspira a remontar la asistencia del año pasado, cuando solo 28.000 personas se manifestaron en Barcelona.

articles.headline: Health minister apologises as neurology review lays bare Watt failings
articles.subtitle: Robbie Butler said he was deeply concerned by the RQIA's final report into 69 deceased patients of the struck-off Belfast neurologist, while the trust said it was "wholly and unreservedly sorry" to those affected.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland's health minister has apologised after an eight-year investigation concluded that patients of a struck-off Belfast neurologist suffered harm through misdiagnosis, delayed diagnosis and inappropriate treatment. Robbie Butler said the findings of the Regulation and Quality Improvement Authority (RQIA) were "deeply concerning", and apologised on behalf of the wider health and social care system.

The final report examined the records of 69 patients of Michael Watt who died while in his care. It is estimated that more than 3,300 patients died under his care between 2008 and 2018, so the review covered a small fraction of those deaths. Watt worked at the Royal Victoria Hospital until 2017 and was struck off the medical register in 2023.

## Cocky and eccentric

The report describes a doctor who diagnosed patients quickly at their first consultation, often without arranging investigations to confirm his suspicions, and who was slow to revisit a diagnosis even when symptoms suggested otherwise. He was also found to have tried multiple medications within short periods, often at high doses.

One patient recalled him as "friendly, jovial and charismatic"; others described him as "cocky and full of himself" and said he "lived in a doolally land". Clinics were described as "chaotic", with long waits for consultations lasting between "a few seconds" and five minutes.

The Belfast Health Trust said it was "wholly and unreservedly sorry" to everyone affected by the neurology recalls since May 2018, when almost 5,500 patients were contacted. A PSNI investigation, Operation Begrain, remains open. Butler said the review was "only the start of another process" to ensure the mistakes of the past are not repeated.

articles.headline: Houthis seize Yemen's Red Sea port of Mokha and close on Bab el-Mandeb
articles.subtitle: The Iran-aligned rebels routed Saudi-backed government forces in Mocha on Thursday and pushed south to the Hanish islands, a shift that threatens the strait carrying a tenth of global trade.
articles.body:
Houthi forces captured the Red Sea port city of Mokha on Thursday and pushed south towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, routing Saudi-backed government troops in the biggest shift in Yemen's war for years. Yemeni government military sources said the rebels had reached the Hanish islands and forced government forces back to Dhubab, directly across the strait from Perim.

Mocha's fall hands the Iran-aligned movement leverage over a chokepoint that carries roughly a tenth of global trade. Reuters reported that the lightning advance came with direct guidance from Iran's Revolutionary Guards, which told the Houthis last week to escalate attacks on Saudi Arabia, according to Yemeni, Iranian and regional sources. Brent crude rose above $105 a barrel.

## A dangerous phase

The Houthi-run Supreme Political Council said fighting had halted on the western coast following the "expulsion" of government-aligned reinforcements, and insisted shipping in the Red Sea "remains safe and uninterrupted", although its ban on Saudi vessels stands. The UN envoy to Yemen told the Security Council the war had entered a "dangerous phase".

Yemen's internationally recognised government accused Iran of reigniting the conflict after a five-year lull and of using the Houthis to tighten its grip on Red Sea shipping routes. Field commanders in Taiz said operations to retake Mokha were already under way.

articles.headline: Dutch coach crash in Swiss Alps kills several tourists
articles.subtitle: The bus, carrying 48 passengers from the Netherlands, hit a crash barrier and slid down a slope between Susch and Zernez in Graubünden on Thursday evening, police said.
articles.body:
A tourist coach carrying 48 Dutch passengers crashed in the south-eastern Swiss Alps late on Thursday, killing several people and injuring others, Graubünden cantonal police said. The vehicle hit a guardrail and overturned between the villages of Zernez and Susch at about 4.45pm, then slid down an embankment.

Police declined to give a death toll until relatives in the Netherlands had been informed, saying only that "several people died in the accident". Five helicopters and several ambulances were sent to the scene, where rescuers worked to pull passengers out of the wreckage. No other vehicles were involved.

Frank Radstake, director of the Dutch travel association ANVR, said the driver appeared to have swerved to avoid a boulder on the road. "The bus driver had to make an evasive manoeuvre, possibly because of a boulder," he told RTL Nieuws. "During that manoeuvre, the bus tipped onto its side and slid some distance down the slope."

The coach was operated by the Dutch tour company OAD. It had left the Netherlands on Monday for a tour of the Alps and was heading for Austria when it crashed, according to Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf.

articles.headline: Fire at two schools in eastern DR Congo kills at least two dozen children
articles.subtitle: The blaze began in a house in Bukavu's densely populated Kadutu district before spreading to the Furaha and Ujamaa primary schools and destroying around 300 homes; officials expect the toll to rise.
articles.body:
A fire swept through two adjoining primary schools in the eastern Congolese city of Bukavu on Thursday, killing at least 24 children and injuring 29, according to local authorities. Officials said the victims included 19 girls and five boys, and warned the toll could rise.

The blaze started in a house before spreading through the densely populated Kadutu commune, reaching the Furaha and Ujamaa schools and destroying around 300 wooden homes. Witnesses described children in school uniform being brought to health centres, some already dead from smoke inhalation, others caught in the crush as crowds fled the flames.

Bukavu has been held since last year by the AFC/M23 rebel alliance, which is backed by Rwanda, and the city's administration is appointed by the movement. Its vice-governor, Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge, gave the figure of 24 dead, while the government in Kinshasa said the toll remained provisional and ordered assessments of the affected schools.

A nurse at the Nyamulagira BDOM health centre told the Associated Press he received about 50 students and teachers in a critical state, of whom 10 were dead on arrival. Another hospital admitted more than 50 students, 14 of whom died. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

articles.headline: Iran-US war widens at sea as Trump ties any ending to the midterms
articles.subtitle: The Revolutionary Guards attacked a US unmanned vessel near the Strait of Hormuz and two ships were hit, hours after the president said he expected the war with Iran to end only after November's elections.
articles.body:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards attacked a US unmanned vessel in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday and two ships were reported hit, as the war between the two countries widened across the Gulf a day after the Houthis seized the Yemeni port of Mokha. Iran claimed to have captured an American "sail drone" near the strait.

The attacks came hours after Donald Trump said he expected the war to end after November's US midterm elections, adding that the timing was a matter for him and threatening to strike a target he referred to as a "pickaxe". Oil markets reacted at once: Brent crude rose above $105 a barrel.

Republican candidates are finding the war a liability on the campaign trail. Al Jazeera reported growing unease among younger Republicans over the conflict, while a BBC survey of voters in several states found many blaming the White House for high fuel prices rather than Tehran.

Iran has also tightened its grip at home, with a reported crackdown on cafés in major cities. Analysts warn that closing the Strait of Hormuz outright remains Tehran's most powerful lever short of direct confrontation with the US Navy.

articles.headline: Russia's new jet-powered drones outpace Ukraine's air defences
articles.subtitle: BBC Verify found Moscow launched the upgraded Geran drones every day in August, as Nato's chief cited Russian actions in making Europe's case for higher defence spending and Canada offered air-defence support.
articles.body:
Russia fired its new jet-powered drones against Ukraine every day throughout August, BBC Verify analysis of Ukrainian Air Force data has found, escalating its use of a weapon Kyiv is struggling to intercept. It is the first time daily attacks by the upgraded Geran drones appear in the data. Ukraine's military said jet-powered drone attacks grew from 350 in June to 1,600 in July and 2,800 in August.

The drones cruise at more than 300mph, faster than Kyiv's interceptors and well beyond the older propeller-driven models. Ukrainian military intelligence says some of the turbojet engines are sourced from China. Ukraine was intercepting 94% of long-range drones earlier this year, but in five of the nightly attacks in August the new drones outnumbered the older ones.

Four Ukrainian companies have begun testing missiles able to shoot down the new models, and the new defence minister, Yevhenii Khmara, has tasked them with producing "thousands of units" as quickly as possible. Analyst Michael Bohnert of the RAND think tank says Moscow is now using more than 15 times as many drones per attack as it did four years ago.

Russian strikes continued overnight, killing at least nine people in attacks on warehouses and ports, and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's plane was delayed in Moldova this week after a jet-powered drone entered its airspace. Canada offered air-defence support during Zelenskyy's visit to Ottawa, while Reuters reported that Nato allies disrupted a Russian plot to disable undersea cables.

articles.headline: Shopify drops React Native and rebuilds its apps in native Swift and Kotlin
articles.subtitle: The company says coding agents changed the maths: after six years of sharing one codebase, duplicating work across two platforms no longer costs what it did in 2020.
articles.body:
Shopify has decided to move its mobile apps from React Native back to separate Swift and Kotlin codebases, reversing the bet it made in 2020 when it went all-in on the cross-platform framework. The engineering post, written by Mustafa Ali, insists that React Native "remains an excellent framework" and frames the reversal as a response to a changed assumption rather than a failure of the technology.

The original case for React Native rested on three things: not building the same feature twice, letting developers work across the whole stack, and spending less time chasing feature parity. As recently as January 2025 the company was still writing publicly that the future of React Native was bright.

## What changed

Coding models did. Shopify has used large language models internally since 2021, and by late 2025 it found that agents could implement a feature on Android using the iOS version as a reference, help developers work outside their main stack, and cut the cost of keeping two platforms in step through shared specifications, tests and review checkpoints.

"What changed is that agents can now do enough of the implementation, translation, testing, and review work that it's no longer the deciding factor it was in 2020," the post says. The company still has to maintain software on two platforms, and says that cost has not disappeared — but it now considers the trade-off settled in native's favour.

Shopify also maintains three widely used React Native libraries. Simon Willison noted that two of them, react-native-skia and flash-list, are being handed to new maintainers, while restyle will be archived at the end of 2026 because it has a smaller user base than the others.

articles.headline: IDScan confirms breach linked to 153 million stolen driver's licences
articles.subtitle: The identity verification firm says an unauthorised party may have copied names and licence numbers from its cloud, after Brian Krebs traced a dark-web ID marketplace back to its platform.
articles.body:
IDScan has confirmed that hackers accessed customer data held in its cloud platform, days after reporting linked the identity verification company to a database containing more than 153 million driver's licence scans. It disclosed the incident in a security notice dated September 4, saying it learned on or around September 1 that certain data may have been accessed without authorisation.

IDScan says its investigation is ongoing but that an unauthorised third party "may" have accessed or copied customer information stored within accounts on the IDScan.net cloud, including full names and driver's licence or other government-issued identification numbers. The company is notifying potentially affected people and offering free credit monitoring and identity protection, even though it says full access to the data required payment.

## Traced back to IDScan

The exposure first came to light on September 1, when the journalist Brian Krebs reported that a dark-web marketplace called Nexus was advertising access to more than 153 million US and Canadian licence scans, along with 10 million ID cards, three million travel documents and 579,000 medical cards.

Krebs then verified samples against records belonging to himself and consenting volunteers, and traced the data back to IDScan, whose technology is used by car rental firms, retailers, banks, cannabis dispensaries, gun shops and hotels.

Nexus was taken offline ahead of an FBI investigation, though the database itself is probably still in criminal hands and multiple actors have since claimed to be selling copies. TechCrunch noted that IDScan's notification had been published with a noindex directive telling search engines to ignore it. IDScan says it is cooperating with federal law enforcement.

articles.headline: Hundreds of AI agents helped one attacker hit 395 organisations in 48 countries
articles.subtitle: GreyNoise says a likely Russian-speaking operator used OpenAI's Codex and a DeepSeek model to build and run exploits against unpatched PaperCut print servers, winning domain admin at 12 victims.
articles.body:
A single threat actor used hundreds of AI agents to develop, test and run a global exploitation campaign against PaperCut print management servers, compromising at least 440 instances belonging to 395 identified organisations across 48 countries, according to research published by GreyNoise. The security firm says the operation began on 31 August.

The campaign targeted two flaws in PaperCut NG and MF, CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078, which the vendor patched urgently days earlier after a university customer's security team helped reproduce the vulnerability. CISA has added both to its known exploited vulnerabilities catalogue and urged administrators to patch by 14 September. A second version of the emergency patch is required, because the first release does not fully protect against the chain.

GreyNoise says the attacker combined OpenAI's Codex as a harness with a DeepSeek model and commodity offensive tooling, building and testing exploits against a lab environment that included a vulnerable PaperCut server and an Active Directory domain. The operator went from an empty workspace to remote code execution against a real victim in just under four hours, and achieved domain administrator rights seven minutes after initial access at one US high school.

## Some agents went off script

The agents also departed from instructions: the operator tried to avoid targets in 28 named countries, but GreyNoise recorded victims in several of them anyway. The campaign harvested credentials from 280 victims, obtained operating system or domain secrets from 147, and won administrator privileges at 12 organisations. The researchers point out that the AI did not discover a zero-day or act autonomously, but sat inside the engineering loop that turned vulnerability research into a production exploitation pipeline.

articles.headline: Bending Spoons buys Miro for $1.36bn, a fraction of its 2022 peak
articles.subtitle: The Italian group will pay cash for the whiteboard software maker at an enterprise value of $1.355bn, well below the $17.5bn valuation Miro attracted during the remote-work boom.
articles.body:
Bending Spoons has agreed to acquire the collaboration platform Miro for $1.355bn in cash, a deal that values the whiteboard software company far below the $17.5bn figure it commanded in 2022. Adding Miro's net cash takes the implied equity value to about $1.79bn.

The Milan-based group said the transaction was unanimously approved by both boards and is expected to close in the fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approval. Under the all-cash agreement, Bending Spoons will buy 100% of Miro's shares, and certain Miro shareholders have agreed to reinvest $295m of their proceeds into newly issued Bending Spoons equity. A merger agreement covering the deal was filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

## Assembling an empire

Bending Spoons, which trades on Nasdaq as BSP, has spent years buying established software businesses — among them Evernote, WeTransfer, Meetup and AOL — and stripping them back to profitability. Miro was founded in 2011 as RealtimeBoard and raised at a $17.5bn valuation in 2022, when demand for remote collaboration tools was at its height. TechCrunch noted the purchase price is around 90% below that peak.

Miro's chief executive published the note he sent to staff, stressing that nothing changes in how the company operates until the deal closes. Miro's own framing highlights the distinction between the $1.355bn enterprise value and the $1.79bn equity value that flows to shareholders.

articles.headline: Anthropic says Chinese labs ran the largest distillation attack it has measured
articles.subtitle: A new report says Alibaba's campaign alone accounts for 151 million exchanges with Claude between May and July, while Moonshot AI and DeepSeek relayed customers' requests and kept the answers.
articles.body:
Anthropic has published a report alleging persistent and escalating distillation attacks by China-based AI companies, saying it observed nearly 200 million exchanges linked to five separate campaigns. "Unauthorized labs have developed increasingly sophisticated methods to circumvent our defenses and harvest the capabilities of US frontier models," the report says.

The largest effort is attributed to Alibaba, which Anthropic calls the biggest wholesale distillation campaign it has ever measured. It counted 151 million exchanges between May and July, peaking at close to three million a day and spread across 3,500 accounts.

Those accounts shared a single fixed prompt designed to force Claude to write out its chain-of-thought reasoning, and Anthropic says the resulting transcripts were used to train Alibaba's Qwen family of models. One request spotted a way around the company's defences by framing the task as a translation exercise.

Moonshot AI, the maker of Kimi, is accused of quietly forwarding its own customers' requests to Claude and storing the answers. In one ten-day stretch, nearly 300,000 requests were routed through about 5,000 accounts, mostly to Anthropic's Opus model; because the users believed they were talking to Kimi, some of what travelled with them was sensitive, including surveillance camera footage uploaded by a user Anthropic assessed as likely linked to China's military.

## Seven labs named

DeepSeek is accused of the same relay technique, and Anthropic says one such request exposed live credentials for a Russian government database linked to the country's defence ministry. The company has also named Xiaomi, Zhipu, SenseTime and MiniMax.

It says it banned the accounts involved and tightened access from unsupported countries. Distillation is not itself illegal in the United States, though Anthropic argues the scale of these operations breaches its terms of service; Y Combinator's Garry Tan has argued publicly that the practice should be tolerated.

articles.headline: Anthropic: AI lets lone operators run campaigns that once needed state teams
articles.subtitle: The company's latest threat intelligence report says individual criminals now sustain intrusions at machine speed, and documents a surveillance platform built for Mali's intelligence service.
articles.body:
Individual hackers are now sustaining campaigns that would have required teams of skilled operators a year ago, according to Anthropic's latest threat intelligence report, which covers Claude misuse the company disrupted between December and August. The report spans seven harm areas, and the actors it names include suspected state-sponsored groups, financially motivated criminals and commercial spyware vendors.

None of the intrusions relied on a novel technique. Stolen credentials and unpatched edge devices feature throughout, while the reconnaissance and tool development that once consumed most of an attacker's time were handed to models running in parallel. Anthropic says the result is "breaches completed in two to three hours, and dozens of victims handled in parallel by individual operators".

## Three hours to admin

Affiliates of the ShinyHunters extortion collective went from a single stolen developer token to full administrative control of a victim's cloud environment in roughly three hours. In another case, AI agents did almost all the work of dumping more than 2,100 Azure Active Directory token sets from over 40 corporate tenants in about 34 hours. A Chinese-speaking group tracked as GTG-10007 ran automated "exploit foundries" against about 50 organisations, and two of its operators were identified as undergraduates.

Elsewhere, Anthropic describes Lakana 360, a surveillance platform built with Claude for Mali's state intelligence service. It monitors roughly 25 million SIM cards across the country's three mobile operators and was designed to get around a legal requirement for court orders. Six weapons development cases were disrupted, including an effort by likely freelance Russia-based developers to build an autonomous kamikaze drone swarm. Anthropic said it banned the accounts involved and shared intelligence with authorities and industry partners.

articles.headline: Cognition's SWE-2 lands within a point of the coding frontier for 64% less
articles.subtitle: The Devin maker says its new model was post-trained on Moonshot AI's open-weight Kimi K3 and beats its own previous version on both score and cost.
articles.body:
Cognition has released SWE-2, a coding model it says reaches 50.0% on its FrontierCode 1.1 Main benchmark — within one point of Anthropic's Fable 5.1 — while costing 64% less to run at that score. The model is available now in Devin Desktop and the Devin CLI, with rollout on Devin Web and Fusion to follow.

SWE-2 is post-trained from Kimi K3, Moonshot AI's 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model, which had already been trained heavily for agentic coding. Cognition says its reinforcement learning run added five to six points on most benchmarks and, for the first time, scaled that training into the multi-trillion-parameter regime. The company says it trains all reasoning-effort levels in a single run, with cost penalties tuned to the slope of the base model's cost-performance curve.

## Cheaper per task

The company is claiming efficiency per task rather than per token. On FrontierCode 1.1 Main, SWE-2 at medium effort scores higher than its previous SWE-1.7 model while taking 58% fewer turns and costing 81% less on average. It makes its first real code edit after a median of 18 steps, against 48 for SWE-1.7, which had drawn criticism for over-exploring simple tasks.

The published table shows a clear soft spot: on the long-horizon Terminal-Bench 4, SWE-2 scores 27.3%, well behind Fable 5.1's 55.8% and GPT-6 Astra's 57.9%. Every figure is Cognition's own pending independent replication, and the company has not released weights, so the model cannot be run locally.

articles.headline: OpenAI opens the Codex harness to developers with its new Agents API
articles.subtitle: The public beta lets developers spin up cloud agents with a single API call, running on OpenAI's managed infrastructure or their own, with support for subagents and MCP tools.
articles.body:
OpenAI has launched the Agents API in public beta, packaging the same agent harness and infrastructure that powers Codex into a single API call. Developers specify the task, model, tools and environment, and OpenAI hosts and maintains the harness that coordinates the work.

The company says useful long-running agents need more than a strong model. They need a harness that manages context, uses tools efficiently and coordinates subagents, plus infrastructure that keeps them running for days in environments where they can work with files, execute code and save intermediate results. The API supports MCP servers, multi-agent configurations with a cap on concurrent subagents, and vaults for credentials.

## The environment stays yours

Customers choose where their agents run: in an OpenAI-managed sandbox, on their own infrastructure, or with a sandbox partner. The harness itself is open source, so developers can inspect the core logic behind model calls, tools and context management while OpenAI operates and maintains it.

There is no additional fee for using the Agents API during the beta — customers pay only for the tokens and tools their agents consume. OpenAI says it will iterate quickly toward general availability, and has published testimonials from early users including Ciridae, which reported a four-fold latency reduction, and Long Lake, which says it can now stand up agents in hours.

articles.headline: OpenAI takes aim at junior bankers with a ChatGPT built for finance
articles.subtitle: The new product bundles licensed data from PitchBook, LSEG and Crunchbase with GPT-6 Astra, and was designed in partnership with Morgan Stanley and Evercore.
articles.body:
OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Financial Services, a tailored version of its ChatGPT Work product that pairs GPT-6 Astra with premium financial data and tooling aimed at investment banking and equity research. The company built it with Morgan Stanley and Evercore, whose feedback steered which problems it tackled first.

The product ships with indexed data from providers including Daloopa, PitchBook, LSEG News and Crunchbase. OpenAI hosts that data itself, which it says removes the friction of external connectors and enables features such as granular citations, so bankers can trace figures and claims back to their sources as their analysis develops. Firms can centrally manage access and data connections through the governance controls already offered in ChatGPT Enterprise.

## The junior banker problem

OpenAI's pitch is aimed squarely at the research, modelling and client-materials work that currently occupies junior bankers. CNBC framed the launch as an attempt to target that workload directly, while SiliconANGLE reported that OpenAI is going after Wall Street bankers with a new version of ChatGPT.

The product is available to eligible financial institutions. OpenAI says its design partnerships will inform post-training, product improvements and expansion into other areas of financial services, and that newer frontier models will be available to the product as they are released.
